chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 5 — Judgment and the Flood
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. The surviving Hebrew text of 11Q12 (11QJubilees), fragment 7, was used for Jubilees 5:1–2 wherever its fragmentary lines preserve wording. The complete chapter and every physical gap follow the Ethiopic (Geʽez) text preserved in manuscripts A–D and printed on text pages 18–21 of R. H. Charles’s 1895 critical edition, The Ethiopic Version of the Hebrew Book of Jubilees. Codicological mapping of the fifth-century Latin manuscript places Jubilees 5 on leaves that are not extant, so it supplies no surviving wording for this chapter. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no wording absent from the primary witnesses was supplied.

verses.text: When humanity’s children began to multiply across the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, the angels of God saw in a certain year of this jubilee that the women were beautiful in appearance. They took wives for themselves from all whom they chose, and the women bore them sons who were giants.
verses.study: The Watchers turn sight and desire into unlawful taking. Their unions violate the boundary of their commission and introduce powerful offspring into an already fallen world.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:1–4 — heavenly beings take wives and the giants appear
Jude 6–7 — angels abandon their proper place and face judgment

verses.text: Lawlessness increased on the earth, and every creature corrupted its way—humanity, livestock, wild animals, birds, and everything that moves upon the earth. All corrupted their ways and their appointed order; they began to devour one another. Violence increased on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of all humanity was continually evil.
verses.study: Corruption spreads from human thought into violence throughout creaturely life. The repeated language of ruined ways shows creation departing from its appointed order.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:5, 11–12 — evil thoughts, violence, and corrupted flesh fill the earth
Romans 8:20–22 — creation shares the bondage and groaning of corruption

verses.text: God looked upon the earth, and it was corrupt. Every creature had corrupted its appointed order, and all who were on the earth had done every kind of evil before his eyes.
verses.study: God’s seeing is a judicial assessment: corruption is comprehensive and openly present before him. Nothing in the earth’s disorder is overlooked.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:12 — God sees that all flesh has corrupted its way
Psalm 14:2–3 — the Lord looks down and finds pervasive turning aside

verses.text: He said that he would destroy humanity and every creature he had made from the face of the earth.
verses.study: The sentence answers the breadth of the corruption. The Creator judges a world that has turned its life-giving order toward violence.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:7 — God declares that he will wipe away humanity and the animals
Isaiah 24:5–6 — the defiled earth suffers under broken covenant order

verses.text: But Noah found favor before the Lord’s eyes.
verses.study: One brief word of favor interrupts the decree of destruction. Preservation begins with grace received, not human power over the coming waters.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:8 — Noah finds favor in the Lord’s eyes
Hebrews 11:7 — Noah responds in faith and becomes an heir of righteousness

verses.text: The Lord was exceedingly angry with the angels he had sent to the earth. He commanded that they be removed from all their authority, and he told us to bind them in the depths of the earth. There they are bound and kept apart.
verses.study: The Watchers lose the authority they abused. Their binding makes clear that heavenly status does not place a rebel beyond divine rule.
crossReferences: 1 Enoch 10:11–14 — the rebellious Watchers are bound beneath the earth
2 Peter 2:4 — sinning angels are confined while awaiting judgment

verses.text: A command went out from before him against their sons: they were to be struck with the sword and removed from beneath heaven.
verses.study: The violent offspring face removal through violence. Their strength cannot withstand the sentence issued from God’s presence.
crossReferences: 1 Enoch 10:9 — the giant offspring are set against one another in destruction
Psalm 37:14–15 — the sword of the wicked turns against them

verses.text: He said, ‘My spirit will not remain with humanity forever, for they are flesh; their days will be one hundred twenty years.’
verses.study: Human life is limited under judgment. Flesh cannot make permanent claims against the Spirit who gives life.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:3 — human days are limited to one hundred twenty years
Isaiah 40:6–8 — flesh fades while God’s word endures

verses.text: He sent his sword among the giants so that each would kill his companion. They began killing one another until they all fell by the sword and were destroyed from the earth.
verses.study: Their mutual violence becomes the means of their undoing. Judgment exposes the self-destroying end of a world ruled by the sword.
crossReferences: Ezekiel 38:21 — every man’s sword is turned against his brother
Matthew 26:52 — those who take the sword perish by the sword

verses.text: Their fathers watched their destruction. Afterward the fathers were bound in the depths of the earth forever, until the day of the great condemnation, when judgment will be carried out against all who corrupted their ways and deeds before the Lord.
verses.study: The Watchers witness the ruin produced by their rebellion before confinement. Present restraint points toward a final and comprehensive judgment.
crossReferences: 1 Enoch 14:4–6 — the Watchers receive a sentence without peace or forgiveness
Jude 6 — rebellious angels are kept in bonds for the judgment of the great day

verses.text: God destroyed them all from their places. Not one remained whom he had not judged according to all his wickedness.
verses.study: Judgment is neither partial nor arbitrary. Each offender is addressed according to actual wickedness.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:5–6 — the way of the wicked perishes under judgment
Revelation 20:12–13 — each is judged according to his deeds

verses.text: He made for all his works a new and righteous nature, so that they would never again sin throughout their whole nature, but would always be righteous, each according to its kind.
verses.study: Judgment is directed toward renewal, not ruin alone. The vision reaches toward creation made stable in righteousness.
crossReferences: Isaiah 65:17 — God promises new heavens and a new earth
2 Peter 3:13 — a new creation is awaited where righteousness dwells
Revelation 21:5 — the enthroned Lord makes all things new

verses.text: The judgment of everything has been established and written in righteousness on the heavenly tablets. This includes everyone who departs from the path appointed for them to walk; if they do not walk in it, judgment is written for every creature and every kind.
verses.study: The appointed path defines faithful creaturely life. Judgment is portrayed as an ordered record rather than an impulsive response.
crossReferences: Psalm 139:16 — ordained days are written in God’s book
Daniel 7:10 — the court sits and the books are opened

verses.text: Nothing in heaven or on earth, in light or darkness, in Sheol or the deep, or in the place of darkness lies outside judgment. Every judgment is established, written, and engraved.
verses.study: No realm offers refuge from moral accountability. The threefold description of the record emphasizes the certainty of judgment.
crossReferences: Psalm 139:7–12 — neither Sheol nor darkness escapes God’s presence
Hebrews 4:13 — every creature is exposed before the one to whom account is owed

verses.text: He will judge everyone: the great according to his greatness, the small according to his smallness, and each according to his way.
verses.study: Difference in rank does not erase responsibility. Judgment considers each person’s actual place and conduct.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 17:10 — the Lord gives to each according to his ways
Luke 12:47–48 — responsibility corresponds to what a servant has received

verses.text: He shows no partiality and accepts no payment when he says he will judge anyone. Even if someone offered everything on earth, he would not show favor, accept the payment, or receive anything from that person’s hand, for he is a righteous judge.
verses.study: Wealth and status cannot purchase escape. The Judge’s righteousness protects judgment from bribery and favoritism.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 10:17 — God shows no partiality and takes no bribe
Job 34:19 — God does not favor the rich over the poor
Romans 2:11 — there is no partiality with God

verses.text: Concerning Israel’s children it has been written and established: if they turn to him in righteousness, he will forgive all their transgressions and pardon all their sins.
verses.study: The certainty of judgment is joined to a genuine path of return. Repentance in righteousness meets divine forgiveness.
crossReferences: 2 Chronicles 7:14 — humble turning receives forgiveness and healing
Ezekiel 18:21–22 — the wicked who turns from sin will live and be forgiven

verses.text: It has been written and established that once each year he will show mercy to all who turn away from all their guilt.
verses.study: Annual mercy places repentance within Israel’s sacred calendar. A recurring appointed day teaches that guilt requires both turning and divine pardon.
crossReferences: Leviticus 16:29–34 — atonement is made once each year for Israel’s sins
Hebrews 9:7 — the high priest enters the inner sanctuary annually with blood

verses.text: Of all who corrupted their ways and thoughts before the flood, no one found favor except Noah alone. Favor was shown to him for the sake of his sons, whom God saved from the floodwaters because of him. Noah’s heart was righteous in all his ways, just as had been commanded concerning him, and he had not departed from anything appointed for him.
verses.study: Noah’s favor bears fruit in obedient life and preservation for his household. The text holds grace, righteousness, and faithful action together.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:9 — Noah is righteous, blameless, and walks with God
Genesis 7:1 — Noah’s household enters the ark because God sees his righteousness
Hebrews 11:7 — Noah’s faith acts on God’s warning

verses.text: The Lord said that he would destroy everything upon the dry land—human beings and livestock, wild animals, birds of the sky, and everything that moves upon the earth.
verses.study: The flood decree reaches the land community corrupted in verse 2. Human rebellion has consequences for the creatures within humanity’s sphere.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:7 — the flood judgment includes humans and land animals
Hosea 4:1–3 — human sin causes the creatures of the land to languish

verses.text: He commanded Noah to make an ark for himself so that he might be saved from the waters of the flood.
verses.study: God provides a concrete means of deliverance before the judgment arrives. Noah must trust the warning enough to build according to command.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:13–18 — God commands Noah to build the ark and establishes his covenant
1 Peter 3:20 — Noah’s household is brought safely through water

verses.text: Noah made the ark in every respect as God had commanded him, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, during the fifth year of the fifth week, at the new moon of the first month.
verses.study: Complete obedience is placed at a precise point in sacred time. The ark exists because Noah does all that God commands.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:22 — Noah does everything God commands
Exodus 40:16–17 — obedient construction is completed at the new year

verses.text: In the sixth year of that jubilee, from the new moon of the second month through the sixteenth day, Noah entered the ark, along with everything we brought to him. On the evening of the seventeenth day, the Lord closed the ark from outside.
verses.study: Divine provision and human obedience meet at the ark’s entrance. God gathers the creatures and closes the final boundary of safety.
crossReferences: Genesis 7:7–10 — Noah’s household and the animals enter before the flood
Genesis 7:16 — the Lord shuts Noah in

verses.text: The Lord opened seven floodgates of heaven and seven mouths of the springs of the great deep.
verses.study: Waters break forth from above and below in a complete undoing of the inhabited world’s boundaries.
crossReferences: Genesis 7:11 — the fountains of the deep and windows of heaven open
Genesis 1:6–10 — creation orders waters above and below and gathers the seas

verses.text: The floodgates began pouring water from heaven for forty days and forty nights, and the springs of the deep also sent up their waters until the whole world was filled with water.
verses.study: The sustained deluge reverses habitable order. Judgment is not momentary but continues until the earth is overwhelmed.
crossReferences: Genesis 7:12, 17 — rain falls forty days and the flood increases
Psalm 104:6 — the deep covers the earth like a garment

verses.text: The waters increased upon the earth. They rose fifteen cubits above every high mountain. The ark was lifted above the earth and moved over the surface of the waters.
verses.study: The same waters that cover every refuge lift the ark. Preservation depends on God’s appointed vessel rather than earthly height.
crossReferences: Genesis 7:18–20 — the ark floats and the waters cover the mountains by fifteen cubits
Psalm 46:1–3 — God remains refuge when waters roar and mountains shake

verses.text: The waters prevailed over the face of the earth for five months—one hundred fifty days.
verses.study: The exact duration underscores the flood’s overwhelming reach and the ordered limit placed upon it.
crossReferences: Genesis 7:24 — the waters prevail for one hundred fifty days
Genesis 8:3 — after one hundred fifty days the waters begin to recede

verses.text: The ark came to rest on the summit of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.
verses.study: After being carried over a world without visible ground, the ark reaches rest. The named mountain marks the first stage of renewed habitation.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:4 — the ark rests on the mountains of Ararat
Psalm 116:7 — the soul is called to return to rest after the Lord’s deliverance

verses.text: At the new moon of the fourth month, the springs of the great deep were closed and the floodgates of heaven were restrained. At the new moon of the seventh month, all the mouths of the earth’s abysses were opened, and the water began descending into the deep below.
verses.study: The sources of judgment are closed, and the waters are directed back into the deep. Restoration begins through the same divine authority that released the flood.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:1–2 — the fountains and windows close and the waters recede
Psalm 104:7–9 — the waters flee and are assigned a boundary

verses.text: At the new moon of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains appeared; and at the new moon of the first month, the surface of the earth became visible.
verses.study: Land returns in measured stages. The sequence echoes creation’s emergence of dry ground from the waters.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:5, 13 — mountain tops and then dry ground become visible
Genesis 1:9–10 — gathered waters reveal the dry land

verses.text: The waters disappeared from upon the earth in the fifth week of the seventh year. On the seventeenth day of the second month, the earth was dry.
verses.study: The calendar records the completion of the waters’ retreat. Judgment has a divinely fixed end, and dry ground is restored for life.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:13–14 — the surface dries and then the earth is fully dry
Habakkuk 3:15 — God treads through the sea in sovereign power

verses.text: On the twenty-seventh day of that month, Noah opened the ark and released from it the wild animals, livestock, birds, and everything that moves upon the earth.
verses.study: The ark opens into a renewed world, and its preserved creatures return to their proper realms. Release turns survival into a new beginning.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:15–19 — Noah’s household and every creature leave the ark
Genesis 1:24–25 — land creatures are ordered according to their kinds

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 5 presents the flood as the response to corruption that crosses both heavenly and earthly boundaries. The Watchers abandon their commission, their giant sons intensify violence, and every creature departs from its appointed way. God’s judgment addresses angels, offspring, humanity, and the disordered creation without granting immunity to rank or strength.

The heavenly tablets express the chapter’s moral order: every path and judgment is recorded, no realm is hidden, and neither partiality nor payment can turn aside the righteous Judge. Yet judgment is not the only word. Those who turn in righteousness receive pardon, and the annual day of mercy teaches Israel to join repentance with God’s provision for atonement.

Noah alone finds favor within the flood generation. That favor is displayed through a righteous heart and precise obedience: he builds, enters, and waits according to command. The ark shows preservation as God’s provision received through faithful action, while the Lord himself gathers the creatures and closes the door.

The flood reverses creation as waters from heaven and the deep cover the mountains, but the reversal is not final. The sources close, the waters descend, land appears, and living creatures emerge from the ark. Judgment clears violent corruption while God preserves a remnant for renewed life.

crossReferences: Genesis 6:1–22 — corruption, Noah’s favor, and the command to build the ark
Genesis 7:1–24 — entry into the ark and the waters’ ascent
Genesis 8:1–19 — the waters recede and the creatures leave the ark
Leviticus 16:1–34 — annual atonement provides cleansing from Israel’s sins
Psalm 104:5–9 — God sets boundaries for the waters
Isaiah 54:9–10 — the waters of Noah become a sign within God’s promise
Matthew 24:37–39 — the flood generation warns of coming judgment
Hebrews 11:7 — Noah obeys the unseen warning by faith
1 Peter 3:18–22 — the ark and flood become a pattern of salvation through judgment
2 Peter 2:4–5 — sinning angels are judged while Noah is preserved
Revelation 20:11–15 — final judgment proceeds according to written records
